outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no event I found settles or moves the topological statement as written. The only event that does (Bryant and Ferry’s counterexamples for every n ≥ 6) was announced in 2018 and had a revised preprint in existence by 30 December 2023, so it predates the window; it has no journal publication or independent verification that I could find. The in-window events are a homology-manifold analogue (Valov, 12 May 2025) and a Busemann G-space special case (Fujioka and Gu, 21 August 2026). No AI system is named in any source I found about this statement.
problem_asks: Statement as given (Wikipedia, January 2024): every n-dimensional homogeneous absolute neighborhood retract is a topological manifold. Unpacked: (0) a universal claim over dimension n: for every n, every n-dimensional homogeneous ANR is a topological manifold (of dimension n). Terms: homogeneous means topologically homogeneous (for any two points some self-homeomorphism carries one to the other); ANR means absolute neighborhood retract, in the literature usually a locally compact, finite-dimensional metric ANR (ANR-compacta or ENRs); n-dimensional means of finite dimension n. Parts by dimension: (a) n = 1; (b) n = 2; (c) n = 3; (d) n = 4; (e) n = 5; (f) n ≥ 6. The bullet asks only the topological-manifold conclusion. Homology-manifold, strongly-locally-homogeneous and aspherical variants are open questions in the literature; I record them as context, not as parts of the bullet.

events.what_happened: R. H. Bing and Karol Borsuk, “Some remarks concerning topologically homogeneous spaces”, Annals of Mathematics 81 (1965) 100–111 (DOI 10.2307/1970385, from a search snippet; journal page not opened). They proved the statement for n = 1 and n = 2, and conjectured it for all n. Wikipedia and Valov’s 2020 survey both state the n = 1, 2 result. I did not open the 1965 paper itself.
events.delivers: Part (a) and part (b): every homogeneous ANR of dimension 1 and every homogeneous ANR of dimension 2 is a topological manifold of that dimension. Nothing for n ≥ 3.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the Bing–Borsuk paper, which contains the n = 1, 2 proofs

events.direction: Supports the statement for n = 1 and n = 2 (proves it there).

events.what_happened: Włodzimierz Jakobsche, “The Bing-Borsuk conjecture is stronger than the Poincaré conjecture”, Fundamenta Mathematicae 106 (1980) 127–134 (DOI 10.4064/fm-106-2-127-134). It shows that a positive answer to the n = 3 case of the statement would imply the Poincaré conjecture. Valov’s surveys also record a construction, under the assumption that the Poincaré conjecture is false, of a 3-dimensional homogeneous compact ANR that is not a manifold.
events.revisions: Wikipedia’s text and Halverson–Repovš give 1978; the journal and Wikipedia’s reference list give 1980. I use 1980.
events.delivers: A reduction only: the n = 3 instance of the statement implies the Poincaré conjecture. It does not settle part (c). Poincaré is now a theorem (Perelman), so the link is historical for the purposes of this record.
events.remains: Parts (c), (d), (e), (f). The converse implication is not established.
events.direction: Neither supports nor cuts against the statement for n = 3; it shows that n = 3 is the case tied to the Poincaré conjecture.

events.what_happened: John Bryant and Steven Ferry announced a counterexample to the Bing–Borsuk conjecture at the Spring Topology Conference in March 2018 (per Valov’s March 2020 survey). John Bryant gave the Florida State colloquium “Some Counterexamples to the Bing-Borsuk Conjecture” on 27 April 2018. Ferry and Bryant gave later talks (Cornell plenary listing, 2019; a Polish congress session in September 2019, from a search snippet only). This is a talk-level announcement; it has no written argument of its own.
events.revisions: Under §5.1 a talk is dated to the write-up. The write-up is the undated preprint in the next event, so this date is the announcement month, kept separately so the announcement is visible. The write-up date is not established.
events.delivers: For every n ≥ 6, the talk abstracts claim infinitely many topologically distinct homogeneous ANR-compacta of dimension n that are not topological manifolds (the FSU abstract says the conjecture is false in dimensions greater than 5; the Cornell listing says every closed simply connected manifold of dimension above 5 has such examples). Parts (f) only.
events.remains: Parts (a) and (b) are untouched; parts (c), (d), (e) are not addressed by the talk abstracts I read.
events.time_since_posted: about 8.5 years since the March 2018 announcement
events.doubts: Talk abstracts only. No written argument was available to me at this stage. The dimension threshold is stated as ‘greater than 5’ in 2018 abstracts and as ‘n ≥ 6’ in later reports, which are the same condition. The Valov 2020 survey records that the example was ‘not published yet’.
events.direction: Cuts against the universal statement for n ≥ 6 (per the abstracts); silent on n = 3, 4, 5.
events.object: Per the FSU abstract (opened): homogeneous spaces homotopy equivalent to the n-sphere for n > 5 that are nowhere locally Euclidean. Per the Cornell 2019 listing (opened, paraphrased): for each closed simply connected manifold of dimension above 5, infinitely many topologically distinct homogeneous ‘fraternal twins’ that are counterexamples; whether compact aspherical counterexamples exist is an open question. Construction type: a modification of the Bryant–Ferry–Mio–Weinberger surgery-theoretic construction of non-resolvable generalized manifolds. The existence proofs are surgery-theoretic and so appear non-constructive; I did not see an explicit object.

events.what_happened: A written preprint by J. Bryant and S. Ferry, cited in Valov’s bibliographies as “An alpha approximation theorem for homology manifolds: counterexamples to the Bing-Borsuk conjecture” (undated; no arXiv number found). Valov’s arXiv 2401.00341 (v1, 30 December 2023, opened) says “Recently, Bryant-Ferry [11] provided a revised version of their paper containing counter-examples to that conjecture”, with n ≥ 6. Valov’s arXiv 2303.10205 (v5, August 2024, opened) cites the preprint as [4] with no year. Valov’s March 2020 survey (arXiv 2003.06907) has no Bryant–Ferry bibliography entry. I did not obtain the preprint text.
events.revisions: The revised version is reported as existing by 30 December 2023 (arXiv 2401.00341 v1). This year is an upper bound on the first public written version, not a first-posting date. No earlier posting date was established. The 2020 survey cites no preprint, so the written version appeared somewhere between March 2020 and December 2023, or cannot be dated more closely.
events.delivers: As reported by Valov (2023 and 2024): for every n ≥ 6, infinitely many topologically distinct homogeneous ANR-compacta of dimension n that are not topological manifolds. The examples are generalized n-manifolds (ENR homology manifolds) with the disjoint disks property. Restrictions: the claim is for n ≥ 6 only; it does not say whether the examples are strongly locally homogeneous, which is an open question Valov records; this is reported from the preprint, which I did not read.
events.remains: Parts (a) and (b) are untouched. Parts (c), (d), (e) remain open per Valov’s 2023 and 2024 texts. Part (f) is refuted for each n ≥ 6 as reported. Open questions recorded in the same sources: whether the counterexamples are strongly locally homogeneous; whether a strongly locally homogeneous counterexample exists; whether compact aspherical counterexamples exist.

checked_by.qualification: Author of several papers and surveys on homogeneous ANR-compacta, including Fund. Math. 2016 and PAMS 2018 papers on this topic
checked_by.what_they_did: Cited and reported the Bryant–Ferry revised version (arXiv 2401.00341, 30 Dec 2023; arXiv 2303.10205 v5, Aug 2024) and its n ≥ 6 claim. The texts I read do not say the construction was verified.

events.time_since_posted: about 2 years 9 months since 30 December 2023 (upper bound on posting); about 8.5 years since the 2018 announcement
events.directly_checkable: Not by hand from what I read. The objects are homology manifolds constructed by surgery.
events.doubts: (1) No journal publication or referee acceptance found. Valov’s 2020 survey called it ‘not published yet’, and his 2023–2024 texts still cite a preprint. (2) No independent expert verification found, and no Lean or Coq check. (3) The preprint text was not retrieved, so the construction and the non-manifold argument are known only through abstracts and survey summaries. (4) The dimension range is reported as ‘above 5’ in talk abstracts and ‘n ≥ 6’ in the surveys. (5) The 2023 text says ‘J. Bryant and S. Ferry announced last year’; read literally that would be 2022, which conflicts with the 2018 start, so I read the phrase as loose wording. (6) The surveys call the examples homogeneous ANR-compacta; whether they meet the statement’s definition of ANR and homogeneity was asserted by those surveys and I did not check it.
events.direction: Cuts against the universal statement for each n ≥ 6, as reported; says nothing about n = 3, 4, 5.
events.object: Infinitely many topologically distinct homogeneous ANR-compacta of dimension n, for each n ≥ 6, that are not topological manifolds (Valov 2024, quoting the preprint). They are generalized n-manifolds with the disjoint disks property, reported as integral ENR homology manifolds in talk listings. The construction modifies the Bryant–Ferry–Mio–Weinberger non-resolvable construction, via surgery; I did not see an explicit object. A talk abstract seen only as a search snippet (not opened) says that for each n ≥ 6 and each k ∈ 1 + 8ℤ there is a topologically homogeneous homology n-manifold with the disjoint disks property, homotopy equivalent to Sⁿ, with Quinn resolution obstruction k, non-resolvable when k ≠ 1. I could not confirm that snippet.

events.what_happened: Vesko Valov, “Local cohomological properties of homogeneous ANR compacta”, arXiv:1411.3422 (v1 13 November 2014, v3 10 August 2015), published in Fundamenta Mathematicae in 2016 (volume 223 in Valov’s bibliography, 233 in the journal URL). Motivated by the Bing–Borsuk conjecture, it shows that for an n-dimensional homogeneous metric ANR compactum each point has a local basis whose closures and boundaries resemble a ball and its boundary sphere cohomologically; that a metric ANR compactum is dimensionally full-valued iff H_n(X, X∖x) is nontrivial for some x; and that every 3-dimensional homogeneous metric ANR compactum is dimensionally full-valued.
events.revisions: v1 13 Nov 2014; v2 3 Feb 2015; v3 10 Aug 2015 (current). Journal: Fund. Math. 2016 (per Valov’s bibliography and the journal URL).
events.delivers: A partial structural result: local cohomological behaviour of homogeneous ANR compacta resembling ℝⁿ, and the dimensional full-valuedness of 3-dimensional homogeneous metric ANR compacta. It does not show any homogeneous ANR is a manifold.
events.remains: Parts (a) and (b) already known. Parts (c), (d), (e), (f) all remain open as far as this paper goes.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper; the volume number differs between sources (223 and 233)

events.direction: Consistent with the statement; yields structural and dimension-theoretic results but no manifoldness conclusion. Neighbouring, not decisive.

events.what_happened: Vesko Valov, “Local homological properties and cyclicity of homogeneous ANR compacta”, arXiv:1605.03263 (v1 11 May 2016; v2 12 December 2017, current). Per Valov’s 2024 bibliography, published in Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 146 (2018) 2697–2705. The abstract says that for an n-dimensional homogeneous metric ANR compactum there is a local basis resembling a ball and its boundary sphere, and that the two Bing–Borsuk questions (cyclicity in dimension n, and no closed acyclic (n−1)-dimensional set separating) both have positive answers simultaneously.
events.revisions: v1 11 May 2016; v2 12 Dec 2017 (current). A search summary reports a later version saying the two questions are ‘simultaneously positive or negative’; I could not confirm that from the v2 abstract.
events.delivers: Answers two other Bing–Borsuk questions (cyclicity and separation) positively, and gives the same local-basis structure as the 2014 paper. Those questions are not parts of the statement, so this does not change the manifold question.
events.remains: All of parts (a) through (f) for the manifold conclusion. Valov notes that a positive answer to either question would resolve another Bing–Borsuk question (whether every finite-dimensional homogeneous metric AR-compactum is a point).

checked_by.who: Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society (journal of record)
checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal publication (2018), per Valov’s 2024 bibliography

events.direction: Neighbouring. Answers different Bing–Borsuk questions in the affirmative; silent on whether homogeneous ANRs are manifolds.

events.what_happened: J. L. Bryant, “Homologically arc-homogeneous ENRs”, Geometry & Topology Monographs 9 (2006) 1–6 (DOI 10.2140/gtm.2006.9.1). Posted to arXiv as 0903.3052 on 17 March 2009. Abstract: “We prove that an arc-homogeneous Euclidean neighborhood retract is a homology manifold.”
events.revisions: Single arXiv version, 17 March 2009; the 2006 journal volume is the earlier appearance.
events.delivers: Homology version only: an arc-homogeneous ENR (a stronger homogeneity hypothesis than topological homogeneity) is a homology manifold. Not a topological manifold conclusion.
events.remains: Every part of the topological statement, (a) through (f), since the conclusion is a different one.

checked_by.qualification: Published proceedings-volume paper; referee arrangements not checked
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (per the arXiv journal reference)

events.direction: Neighbouring: a homology-manifold conclusion under a stronger homogeneity hypothesis. Consistent with the statement but does not reach it.

events.what_happened: John L. Bryant, Steven C. Ferry, Washington Mio and Shmuel Weinberger, “Topology of homology manifolds”, arXiv:math/9304210 (posted 1 April 1993), Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (N.S.) 28 (1993) 324–328. Abstract: “We construct examples of nonresolvable generalized n-manifolds, n ≥ 6, with arbitrary resolution obstruction”, homotopy equivalent to any simply connected closed n-manifold. A longer version appeared in the Annals in 1996 (per Valov’s 2020 bibliography). This is the foundation the Bryant–Ferry counterexamples modify.
events.revisions: Single arXiv version 1 April 1993; BAMS 1993; Annals 143 (1996) 435–467 per Valov 2020.
events.delivers: Non-resolvable generalized n-manifolds for n ≥ 6. The paper makes no homogeneity claim, so it does not bear on whether they are homogeneous ANRs, and so is not a counterexample to the statement by itself.
events.remains: All parts (a) through (f) of the topological statement.

checked_by.who: Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society (journal of record)

events.direction: Neighbouring. Supplies non-resolvable building blocks in n ≥ 6, but says nothing about homogeneity, so it cuts neither way on the statement by itself.
events.object: Non-resolvable generalized n-manifolds for n ≥ 6, homotopy equivalent to any simply connected closed n-manifold, with arbitrary resolution obstruction. Constructed by surgery theory, so existence is non-constructive. They are not claimed to be homogeneous.

events.what_happened: Vesko Valov, “Local structure of homogeneous ANR-spaces”, arXiv:2303.10205 (v1 17 March 2023; v2 1 April 2023; v3 21 April 2023; v4 8 June 2023; v5 2 August 2024). Published online in Transactions of the AMS in October 2024 (per a search summary; journal page not opened). It gives a positive answer to whether every finite-dimensional homogeneous metric ANR compactum is dimensionally full-valued, and describes the local structure of finite-dimensional homogeneous locally compact ANR-spaces.
events.revisions: v1 17 Mar 2023; v2 1 Apr 2023; v3 21 Apr 2023; v4 8 Jun 2023; v5 2 Aug 2024 (current, as fetched). TAMS online Oct 2024 (search summary).
events.delivers: Dimension-theoretic: every finite-dimensional homogeneous metric ANR compactum is dimensionally full-valued, plus local structure results. It does not assert or prove that such spaces are topological manifolds.
events.remains: All of parts (a) through (f) for the manifold conclusion. The v5 text also records that counterexamples exist and that the statement is ‘still open in dimensions 3, 4 and 5’ with the Bryant–Ferry counterexamples in mind.

checked_by.who: Transactions of the American Mathematical Society (journal of record)
checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal publication (online October 2024, per a search summary)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (journal page not opened)

events.direction: Neighbouring: dimension-theoretic property of homogeneous ANR compacta; consistent with the statement but not a step toward manifoldness.

events.what_happened: Vesko Valov, “Homology manifolds and homogeneous compacta”, arXiv:2505.07196 (v1 12 May 2025; the only version). No journal reference. It gives a necessary and sufficient condition (B(n−1)) for a locally compact homogeneous ANR-space to be an almost homology n-manifold, and an analogous statement for strongly locally homogeneous LC^(n−1)-spaces. It states a homology version of the Bing–Borsuk conjecture as a conjecture (every n-dimensional homogeneous ANR-space is a homology n-manifold), citing Bryant’s 2002 talk, and the homogeneity conjecture for ANR homology (n ≥ 5)-manifolds with the disjoint disks property, citing Bryant–Ferry–Mio–Weinberger.
events.delivers: Homology version only: a characterisation of when locally compact homogeneous ANR-spaces (and strongly locally homogeneous LC^(n−1)-spaces) are almost homology n-manifolds, via condition B(n−1). It does not state or prove that homogeneous ANRs are topological manifolds, and the paper explicitly is about homology manifolds.
events.remains: All of parts (a) through (f) for the topological-manifold conclusion. The homology version (its own conjecture) is also not established.
events.doubts: A later paper that describes the Bing–Borsuk conjecture only in its modified homology form, and, on the fetched summary, does not mention the Bryant–Ferry counterexamples (the summary says it does not name them as Bryant–Ferry). I could not confirm this against the full text, because the fetch returned a summary rather than the paper.
events.direction: Analogue: relates the statement to its homology version. Neither confirms nor refutes the topological statement.

events.what_happened: Tadashi Fujioka and Shijie Gu, “Busemann G-spaces with convex balls”, arXiv:2608.20800 (v1 21 August 2026; v2 14 September 2026, which added Corollary 1.2 and Remarks 1.4, 1.5 and 3.8). Main result: any Busemann G-space in which every sufficiently small metric ball is convex is a topological manifold. The key ingredient is Ivanov’s Helly theorem. The appendix gives a counterexample to a question of Berestovskii, Halverson and Repovš.
events.delivers: A manifold conclusion for a restricted class: Busemann G-spaces with convex small balls. The introduction (opened) says every G-space is topologically homogeneous, and treats the Busemann manifold question as a special case of the Bing–Borsuk conjecture in the Halverson–Repovš survey. The theorem assumes no finite-dimensionality. The introduction also treats finite-dimensionality of G-spaces as open in general, so whether the conclusion gives a fixed dimension n (needed for parts (c)–(f)) is not established by what I read. The paper does not mention Bing–Borsuk.
events.remains: Parts (a) through (f) for general homogeneous ANRs. For the convex-ball G-spaces, the dimension and ANR status are not shown, so the overlap with (c)–(f) is unclear.
events.direction: Restricted special case of the manifold question for a class of homogeneous spaces, in the direction of the statement (manifold conclusion). Whether it reaches the Bing–Borsuk statement depends on dimension and ANR status, which the paper does not state as far as I read.

events.what_happened: Yibo Ji, “An AI Generated Counterexample to Borsuk Problem in Dimension 63”, arXiv:2608.12561 (v1 12 August 2026; v2 14 August 2026, marked withdrawn by the author). It claims a 321-point set in ℝ⁶³ that cannot be partitioned into 64 subsets of smaller diameter, proving b(63) ≥ 65. This is Borsuk’s partition problem, not the Bing–Borsuk conjecture. It surfaced under my AI search for this statement and is recorded as a discarded neighbouring event.
events.delivers: For Borsuk’s partition problem only, if correct: a counterexample in dimension 63. Nothing about homogeneous ANRs or manifolds.
events.remains: All of the Bing–Borsuk statement, parts (a) through (f).
events.directly_checkable: Yes for Borsuk’s partition problem: the 321-point set is explicit, per the abstract. Not checked by me. Not relevant to this statement.
events.doubts: The page’s comments say the same counterexample was already posted at two other locations. The author withdrew v2. Otherwise not reviewed.

events.direction: For Borsuk’s partition problem, against the conjecture if correct. No bearing on the Bing–Borsuk statement.
events.object: A 321-point set in ℝ⁶³ that cannot be partitioned into 64 pieces of smaller diameter, built from the G₂(4) Euclidean representation and a Jenrich–Brouwer 320-point core in dimension 63 by adding one projected and rescaled point. Explicit, per the abstract.

summary: Built from 39 WebSearch queries and about 40 fetches. PDFs mostly did not render through the fetch tool, so most text comes from arXiv HTML and abstract pages and from fetch-tool summaries; quoted text should be checked against the sources before it is relied on. The statement is the universal claim that every n-dimensional homogeneous ANR is a topological manifold. Its only settled cases are n = 1 and n = 2 (Bing and Borsuk, 1965; Wikipedia and Valov 2020). For n = 3 the statement implies the Poincaré conjecture (Jakobsche, 1980), and n = 3 is open. Bryant and Ferry announced, at the Spring Topology Conference in March 2018, a counterexample for every n ≥ 6 (talk abstracts say ‘dimensions greater than 5’); the examples are generalized manifolds with the disjoint disks property, built by modifying the Bryant–Ferry–Mio–Weinberger non-resolvable construction. The written preprint, “An alpha approximation theorem for homology manifolds: counterexamples to the Bing-Borsuk conjecture”, is undated and I did not obtain it. Valov’s arXiv survey of 30 December 2023 reports a revised version already in existence, so this event predates the window; it is dated 2023 as an upper bound because no first posting date was found. Valov’s March 2020 survey called the example ‘not published yet’. I found no journal acceptance, no independent expert verification and no Lean or Coq check through 11 October 2026. Valov’s 2023–2024 papers cite it as a report; his 2025 homology paper, on the fetched summary, does not mention the counterexamples. On the statement as written, the counterexamples would refute it for each n ≥ 6, while n = 3, 4, 5 remain open per the same sources. Wikipedia’s article (last edited 6 July 2025) mentions none of this: its lead says only that the conjecture is proved for dimensions 1 and 2, and it has no status section. In the window, Valov (12 May 2025) gives a homology-manifold characterisation of homogeneous ANR spaces, which is an analogue and not the topological statement. Fujioka and Gu (21 August 2026) prove that Busemann G-spaces with convex small balls are topological manifolds. Halverson–Repovš list the Busemann conjecture as a special case of Bing–Borsuk, but the 2026 introduction does not say how the two relate, and the paper does not state a fixed dimension. AI: none of the Bing–Borsuk sources names an AI system. The AI-credited items that surfaced are Ji (arXiv 2608.12561, withdrawn 14 August 2026, citing GPT 5.6 Sol) and Grinsztajn (May 2026, citing GPT-5.5 Pro per Wikipedia; GitHub not opened). Both concern Borsuk’s partition problem, a different problem, and are recorded as discarded neighbouring events. Source discrepancies: Jakobsche’s year (1978 in Wikipedia’s text and in Halverson–Repovš, 1980 in the journal); the threshold for the homogeneity conjecture for DDP homology manifolds (n ≥ 5 in Valov 2020 and 2025; n ≥ 7 in a search snippet quoting another paper, not opened); the volume of Valov’s 2016 Fundamenta paper (223 in his bibliography, 233 in the journal URL); and the 2016 cyclicity paper’s v2 abstract (both questions have positive answers simultaneously), against a search summary that reports a later version saying ‘positive or negative’, which I could not confirm.
competing_reading: The strongest case for reading the record differently: the Bryant–Ferry counterexamples are announced and cited but unpublished as far as I can find, with no expert verification and with the preprint text unread, so the universal statement could be counted as still open rather than refuted. Separately, the bullet quantifies over n, and n = 3, 4, 5 are open on every source, so a per-dimension reading (proved for n ≤ 2, open for 3–5, refuted for n ≥ 6) gives a different count from a universal reading (false). The Fujioka–Gu result could be read as a case of the statement if its conclusion gives a dimension and ANR status; I did not establish either.
what_would_settle_it: (i) The Bryant–Ferry preprint itself: its public identifier, first posting date, the proof of homogeneity and non-manifoldness for n ≥ 6, and its exact dimension range. (ii) A journal acceptance, a published verification, or a review (for example in MathSciNet or zbMATH) of that preprint. (iii) Whether Fujioka and Gu’s conclusion gives a fixed dimension and ANR status for the G-spaces they cover. (iv) Whether the Bryant–Ferry talk slides and the 2019 Polish and Texas abstracts agree on the dimension threshold. (v) The 1965 Bing–Borsuk paper itself, to confirm the n = 1, 2 scope.

judgement.why: The statement is a single universal claim, so a counterexample in any dimension refutes it outright; the Bryant–Ferry n ≥ 6 counterexamples are therefore scored whole/refuted/counterexample, but both their announcement (March 2018) and the written preprint (in existence by 30 December 2023 per Valov) predate the snapshot, and they remain unreviewed (cited and reported by Valov, not verified), so they tier only as a pre-snapshot claim. Bing–Borsuk 1965 settles n = 1, 2 (case, digested). Jakobsche, BFMW and Valov's dimension-theoretic papers prove no manifold conclusion (none); Bryant 2006 and Valov 2016/2025 address homology or other Bing–Borsuk questions (variant). The only in-window event on the topic, Fujioka–Gu, proves manifoldness for Busemann G-spaces with convex balls, with no established finite dimension or ANR status, so it is a variant rather than a case. Ji and Grinsztajn concern Borsuk's partition problem, a different problem (F15), and are variants; their AI roles are recorded from their own quotes but cannot touch this statement.
judgement.doubts: Close call on the Bryant–Ferry scope: a per-dimension reading would make it a case (n ≥ 6) rather than whole; either way it is pre-snapshot and unreviewed, so it does not affect the post-2024 count. Its written version's first posting date is only bounded above by December 2023; if it was in fact first posted after 26 January 2024 the conclusion would change, but the record shows Valov citing a revised version on 30 December 2023. The Grinsztajn AI attribution rests on Wikipedia, not the author's own account.
